summary: Robert van Gulik was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (~1929–1934) and Utrecht University (~1934–1935), completing his doctoral studies under Jan Gonda (~1930–1935).

Robin Coningham is a scholar of Indology and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin (~1989–1994) and held professorships at the University of Bradford (1994–2005) and Durham University (from 2005).
Robin D. S. Yates is a historian and Sinologist. He earned his PhD from Harvard University (~1975–1980) and held a James McGill Professorship at McGill University from ~1993 to 2021.

Robin Dunbar studied at Magdalen College, Oxford (~1966–1969) and completed his doctoral studies under John Hurrell Crook (~1969–1974). He later held a position at University College London from ~1987 to 1994.

Roderick M. Chisholm was a philosopher who studied at Brown University and earned his PhD at Harvard (~1938–1942). He held professorships at the Barnes Foundation (~1945–1946) and Brown University (~1947–1986), also serving as Metaphysical Society of America president (1973).

Roderick S. Bucknell was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He served on the faculty at the University of Queensland from ~1976 to 2002, where he was an Associate Professor (attested 1999–2000).

Roderick Whitfield is a scholar of Sinology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the British Museum (attested 1986) and SOAS University of London, where he was an emeritus professor (attested 2011).
Roger Brown was a linguist who completed his studies at the University of Michigan (~1945–1952). He subsequently held a long-term academic appointment at Harvard University from 1962 to 1994.

Roger Caillois was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and École Pratique des Hautes Études under Marcel Mauss (~1933–1938), later holding a post at the United Nations (~1948–1971).

Roger Heim studied at École Centrale Paris (~1920–1923) and the Science Faculty of Paris. He worked at the Muséum national d'histoire naturelle (~1929–1970), serving as director of the National Museum of Natural History (~1950–1965).

Roger R. Jackson was a Buddhist and Tibetan studies scholar. He completed his MA and PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa (~1974–1983) and taught religion at Carleton College (~1989–2016).

Roger T. Ames is a philosopher and Sinologist who earned his PhD from SOAS under D. C. Lau (1975–1978). He spent his primary career at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1978–2016) and served as Fulbright Professor at Peking University (~2016).
Rohit Saluja works in the fields of computational studies and Indology. He has held posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.

Roland Barthes was a French philosopher and linguist. He studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris under Émile Benveniste, later holding posts at CNRS (~1952–1959), the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (~1962–1977), and the Collège de France (1976–1980).

Roland Ferenczi is an Indologist and historian. His academic posts include serving as a visiting lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University and as a project researcher at the University of Hamburg (both attested 2026).
Roland Steiner is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. He studied under Michael Hahn (attested 1990) and served as an assistant professor at the University of Marburg (attested 2002).

Roland Wenzlhuemer is a historian who earned his doctorate from the University of Salzburg and completed his habilitation at Heidelberg University. He held professorships at Heidelberg University (2014) and the University of Munich (2017).

Rolf Alfred Stein was a Sinologist and Tibetologist who studied under scholars including Marcel Granet and Paul Pelliot. He was a directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1951–1975) and a professor at the Collège de France (1965–1982).
Rolf Scheuermann is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Helmut Tauscher (attested 2010).

Romila Thapar is a historian of ancient India who completed her doctorate at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham (~1955–1958). She held professorships at the University of Delhi (1963–1970) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (1970–1991, 1993).
